transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
Hurricane Isaias has made landfall tonight in the Florida panhandle.
As NPR's Debbie Elliott reports, it was a Category 2 hurricane, bringing with it 105-mile-an-hour winds.
The National Weather Service says the eye of Hurricane Isaias came ashore near Destin, Florida.
This storm weakened slightly from a major Category 3 hurricane to a Category 2 ahead of landfall.
But winds were still powerful enough to down trees and knock out power lines in its path.
Widespread power outages are reported in South Alabama and northwest Florida.
Flash flood warnings are posted along the storm's path as it moves inland,
where it's expected to produce tropical storm-force winds and tornadoes across the southeastern U.S.
Isaias is the first hurricane of the Atlantic season.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Questview, Florida.
President Trump says Russia will supply about 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the U.S.
He says it's an effort to lower rising diesel prices.
As NPR's Emily Fang reports, Trump says he and Russian leader Vladimir Putin reached that agreement by phone today.
It's unclear if importing Russian diesel flies in the face of a new law Trump just signed into effect.
Named in honor of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, the law put 500 percent tariffs on Russian imports
and personally sanctioned Putin.
The U.S. Treasury Department has, however, just temporarily paused its sanctions on Russian diesel.
Trump has also temporarily paused a federal tax on diesel, though some state taxes may still remain,
all in an effort to rein in diesel prices that have shot up as much as 70 percent since the war with Iran.
These measures will likely not bring diesel prices down, however.
For example, the diesel Russia will provide amounts to just a few days of American national diesel consumption.
Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump has selected a new press secretary. He named Katie Zacharia to the post today.
She'll succeed former press secretary Caroline Levitt, who left that position in August.
NPR's Deepa Shivram has more on that story.
Zacharia is a political commentator and an adviser with Trump's media and technology group,
which runs Trump's social media site, Truth Social.
She also briefly served as a spokesperson at the Department of Homeland Security.
It's not clear when her first day in the role would be or when the first press briefing would be.
Those briefings have largely been on hold since Levitt left the position earlier this year.
Trump's selection of a new press secretary comes as the president and his party are facing headwinds in the upcoming midterm elections.
On social media, Trump says he's confident Zacharia will deliver, quote, strong results for our country and calls her a loyal and brilliant supporter.
Deepa Shivram, NPR News, the White House.
Stocks closed up on Wall Street today with the Dow up 423 points. And you're listening to NPR News.
Hall of Fame tight end and Super Bowl winning coach of the Chicago Bears Mike Ditka has died.
He was 86 years old.
As Noah Jennings of member station WBEZ reports, his look was just as legendary as his football career.
Mike Ditka was more than a coach. He was a symbol.
His signature style, the mustache, aviator sunglasses and sweater vest inspired the recurring Saturday Night Live sketch of the Bill Swersky superfans.
And Ditka, being the bold, outspoken person he was, appeared on the sketch once in 1993, just days after he was fired from the Bears.
Look, this is Mike Ditka. Let's get it done, sweetheart.
And you can take this to the bank, my friends.
Live from New York, it's Saturday night.
Ditka's likeness will live on at Bears Games as fans continue filling the stands every Sunday in his iconic outfit.
For NPR News, I'm Noah Jennings in Chicago.
A second powerful earthquake has hit Panama. The 6.6 magnitude quake followed a Friday morning quake of 7.7 magnitude.
In between the two were several aftershocks. The quakes were centered south of the capital of Panama City where most of the reported damage has occurred.
Some buildings collapsed near the quake's epicenter and evacuations took place across the country. The country's president is appealing for calm.
Residents of the Brazilian city of Manaus are struggling to breathe this weekend as wildfires from the Amazon are sending smoke into the area.
Health officials say pollutants have reached 196 micrograms per cubic meter. The normal range is from 3 to 9 micrograms.
Government workers were sent home on Friday because of the smoke.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
Get your free guide at netsweet.com/story.

topics.text: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida panhandle as Category 2 storm, knocking out power
Trump says Russia will supply 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to lower U.S. prices
Trump names Katie Zacharia as new White House press secretary, succeeding Caroline Levitt
Stocks close higher on Wall Street, with the Dow up 423 points
Hall of Fame coach Mike Ditka, Super Bowl winner with Chicago Bears, dies at 86
Second powerful earthquake of magnitude 6.6 strikes Panama after 7.7 quake Friday
Wildfire smoke from the Amazon pushes pollution in Brazil's Manaus city to dangerous levels
